statement: GBD 2021: 17.6M cases (15.8-20.3), age-standardised prevalence 208.8/100k, +14.1% since 1990, F:M 2.45, projected 31.7M by 2050
Anti-CCP and RF detectable in stored blood a median 2.5 years before symptom onset; ACPA seropositivity precedes clinical RA by 3-5 years on average
HLA-DRB1 shared epitope x smoking for ACPA-positive RA: RR 8.7 (5.7-13.1); attributable proportion due to interaction 0.4-0.6
GWAS meta-analysis 29,880 cases / 73,758 controls: 101 loci, 98 candidate genes; RA loci enriched for approved drug targets
Silica RA OR 1.94 (1.46-2.58) in both seropositive and seronegative disease; 31-study review of silica, asbestos, solvents, pesticides, animal dust, exhaust: RR 1.25-1.49
TICORA: good response 82% vs 44%, DAS28 remission 65% vs 16%
BeSt 2-year: all four strategies converged at 42% remission; initial combination better suppressed joint damage
NORD-STAR 48-wk CDAI remission: abatacept 59.3%, certolizumab 52.3%, tocilizumab 51.9%, active conventional 39.2%
2011 ACR/EULAR provisional definition; 2022 Boolean2.0 (PtGA <=2 cm) raised 6-month remission from 14.8% to 20.6% (early) and 4.2% to 6.0% (established) with no loss of predictive value

item: Remission is not absence of disease
statement: Power Doppler positivity in clinical remission: flare OR 4.52 (2.61-7.84), progressive erosion OR 12.80; ACPA+ memory B cells persist activated in clinical remission including under JAK inhibition
55-record systematic review: residual disability, tender/swollen joints, pain, fatigue and impaired patient global persist in a substantial fraction meeting remission or LDA targets

item: Refractory disease is a minority but not rare
statement: 23 studies, 27,987 patients: D2T prevalence 11.7% (9.5-14.3); >=3 b/tsDMARD failures 4.3%; >=4 failures 1.6%; poly-refractory 2.7%
Among D2T patients with ultrasound, 57% persistent inflammatory refractory (PIRRA) and 43% non-inflammatory refractory (NIRRA); NIRRA had higher BMI and fibromyalgia prevalence
34.2% of 187 RA patients met 2016 FM criteria; FM independently associated with higher DAS28-CRP driven by subjective components, worse QoL, and more corticosteroid use despite less DMARD use
COMORA (3,920 patients, 17 countries): depression 15%, asthma 6.6%, MI/stroke 6%, solid malignancy 4.5%, COPD 3.5%
Meta-SMR for cardiovascular mortality 1.50 (1.39-1.61); ischaemic heart disease 1.59; cerebrovascular 1.52

item: RA-ILD is a major mortality driver
statement: Denmark: RA-ILD in 2.2% of incident RA; 1-year mortality 13.9% vs 3.8%, 10-year 60.1% vs 34.5%

Serious infection vs csDMARDs: standard-dose biologics OR 1.31 (1.09-1.58), high-dose 1.90 (1.50-2.39). ORAL Surveillance: tofacitinib vs TNFi MACE HR 1.33 (0.91-1.94), cancer HR 1.48 (1.04-2.09), non-inferiority not shown
Single-cell atlas, 79 donors, >314,000 cells: six cell-type abundance phenotypes spanning lymphocyte-rich to lymphocyte-poor, dynamic and associated with treatment response
COVAD-2 (n=1,997): advanced therapy use 29.6% overall; 44.0% Europe, 11.7% Asia, 5.3% Africa; 2.7% in low-HDI vs 38.8% in very-high-HDI countries

item: Most guidance rests on low-certainty evidence
statement: 2021 ACR guideline: 44 recommendations, 7 strong and 37 conditional. EULAR points to consider for D2T RA: strength of recommendation C-D throughout

item: Patients and physicians do not measure the same thing
statement: 73 blinded RCTs, 165 comparisons, 33,956 patients: physician global SMD -0.60 vs patient global -0.50; DeltaSMD -0.09 (-0.12 to -0.05), driven by swollen joint count; pain independently associated only with patient global
Cochrane 7 RCTs, 732 pts: ACR50 RR 3.0 (1.5-6.0) at 52 wk. Remission in at most about half of patients across RCTs
Cochrane 6 RCTs, 468 pts: SMD -0.49 joints, -0.42 pain, ESR -17.6 mm; withdrawal for adverse reactions OR 3.0
Cochrane 4 RCTs, 300 pts: SMDs -0.33 to -0.52; weakest csDMARD for disease activity, retained for combination use and metabolic effects
RACAT/TEAR: 78% vs 63% still on assigned therapy at 1 year vs MTX+etanercept
Cochrane living NMA, 19 RCTs, 4,779 pts: untried TNFi ACR50 OR 6.04 (2.49-16.3) high certainty; IL-6 inhibitors, abatacept, rituximab and JAK inhibitors also moderate-to-high certainty
TICORA and BeSt: intensive targeted control outperforms routine care on remission and damage
Very early (median 3 mo) vs late early (12 mo) DMARD start: DAS28 improvement 2.8 vs 1.7 at 36 months with less radiographic progression
Erosion healing 20% vs 6% at 24 months (p=0.045), with no effect on inflammation
Cochrane 24 studies, 2,882 pts: SMD -0.36 (-0.62 to -0.10), 14.4 points on a 100-point scale, NNTB 7 — the best-evidenced fatigue intervention in RA
Same Cochrane review: SMD -0.24 (-0.40 to -0.07), NNTB 10
10 RCTs, 547 pts: isokinetic strength +23.7%, isometric +35.8% (both P<0.001); RAPIT high-intensity weight-bearing exercise slowed hip bone loss over 2 years
Cochrane 5 RCTs, 2,876 pts: ACR20 38% vs 23%, ACR50 18% vs 7%, ACR70 7% vs 2% — works, displaced by more effective agents
31 RCTs, 2,776 pts: ACR20 RR 1.55 (1.14-2.13), ACR50 RR 2.04, ACR70 RR 2.19 (GRADE high), DAS28 WMD -1.65, adverse events no different from MTX alone
ACR20 RR 1.44 (1.28-1.62), ACR50 RR 1.88, ACR70 RR 2.12; independent meta-analysis remission RR 1.31 (1.11-1.55) — but efficacy correlated negatively with trial quality in the same analysis

item: TwHF monotherapy is non-inferior to methotrexate
statement: 19 RCTs, 1,795 participants: ACR20 RR 1.06 (0.90-1.26) and ACR50 RR 1.03 (0.80-1.34), both moderate GRADE certainty
RESET-RA, 242 pts refractory to b/tsDMARDs: ACR20 35.2% vs 24.2% sham at 3 months (p=0.0209); related serious adverse events 1.6%
GLORIA, 451 pts aged 65+: DAS28 0.37 lower (p<0.0001) and damage 1.7 points lower (p=0.003); adverse events of interest 60% vs 49%, adjusted RR 1.24 (p=0.02)

Cochrane 2 RCTs, 84 pts: no significant difference on ESR, CRP, VAS global, swollen or tender joints, GHQ or DAS. A CAM systematic review found no significant pain difference across 3 sham-controlled trials
Within a positive 32-RCT network meta-analysis, no acupuncture-related therapy outperformed DMARDs alone for morning stiffness
7 RCTs in chronic pain: d = -0.11 (-0.96 to 0.74), P=0.31; adverse events IRR 1.4 (1.12-1.75). No RA-specific trial exists
Sensitive joints MD -1.66 (-6.32 to 2.99), I2=93% — no benefit
Cochrane 2015, 9 studies, 579 pts: pain MD 0.50 (-0.84 to 1.84) at very low level of evidence
Cochrane dietary manipulation review: no difference in pain, function or stiffness
94 seropositive patients, 12 weeks, double-blind: only subjective improvement overall, no difference between allergen-free and allergen-restricted diets
Cochrane: 2 studies, 57 patients, no evidence of benefit at very low certainty — despite smoking being an established causal risk factor
n=23: 1 responder vs 0 on placebo
SMD -0.01 — no effect

item: TwHF monotherapy as an improvement on methotrexate
statement: Non-inferior, not superior: ACR20 RR 1.06 (0.90-1.26)

item: Iguratimod monotherapy as an improvement on methotrexate
Methotrexate + glucocorticoid to prevent RA in ACPA-positive at-risk individuals
statement: TREAT EARLIER: no prevention at 2 years (19% vs 18%, HR 0.81); at 5 years ACPA-positive 58% vs 65%, HR 0.7 — no effect
APIPPRA: primary endpoint met on treatment (6% vs 29%) but 25% vs 37% progressed by 24 months; ALTO extension at median 55 months shows a 4.9-month arthritis-free survival difference that diminished
PRAIRI: single 1000 mg infusion delayed arthritis onset by 12 months, HR 0.45 (0.154-1.322) — delay, not prevention
ARCTIC REWIND: flare in 27/43 (63%) vs 2/41 (5%) on stable therapy; risk difference 58% (42-74) — not non-inferior
Early ACR20 signal did not sustain across outcomes; no drug emerged
Symptomatically effective short-term; at 10 years 7/10 irradiated patients had died vs 2/9 controls, with 3 B-cell malignancies
Cochrane 11 studies, 672 pts: global impression RR 1.44 (1.03-2.03) but adverse events OR 3.90 (2.31-6.56); only one 20-patient study of a strong opioid

Null vs same-acupoint sham (Cochrane) but SMD -1.11 (conventional) to -1.42 (electroacupuncture) vs conventional therapy and non-acupoint sham in a 10-RCT network meta-analysis. The dispute is about which sham is a valid control, not about the data

DAS-28 WMD -0.83 (-1.38 to -0.28) at self-declared moderate certainty in one meta-analysis; no significant effect on RA pain across 27 RCTs in another. May be outcome-specific rather than a true contradiction

item: Vitamin D and omega-3 for prevention
statement: VITAL (n=25,871): on treatment vitamin D HR 0.78 (0.61-0.99) and omega-3 HR 0.85 (0.67-1.08); two years after stopping, vitamin D HR 0.98 (0.83-1.17) and omega-3 HR 0.83 (0.70-0.99). Endpoint is all autoimmune disease, not RA

Cochrane: Cretan Mediterranean pain MD -14.00/100 (-23.6 to -4.37) and fasting+vegetarian pain MD -1.89/10; an overview of systematic reviews concludes little or no difference at low certainty; 7-RCT pooling gives pain -9.22 mm at very low certainty

Atorvastatin add-on DAS28 SMD -2.00 (-3.19 to -0.81) across 15 RCTs; parallel review -2.46 with I2=97%. An effect larger than most biologics from a lipid-lowering drug is more plausibly a pooling artefact
evidence_tier: Uncertain (effect size not credible as stated)

statement: Meta-analysis of 21 studies OR 4 (1.2-14) for knee response at 6 months; a 97-patient RCT found 48% response in both arms

Trial-level pooling reassuring (infection RR 1.37, liver RR 1.14, renal RR 2.20, none significant) against 40 years of toxicology documenting oligospermia, testicular atrophy, amenorrhoea and infertility. Short trials in older cohorts cannot detect gonadal toxicity
DAS28 MD -1.20 (-1.85 to -0.55) from 6 publications the authors describe as low quality — a biologic-sized effect from six small trials
Tender joint count SMD -0.59 (-0.79 to -0.39) across 18 RCTs, 1,018 pts, with no significant effect on DAS28, ESR or CRP — symptom effect without inflammatory effect
IL-6 SMD -0.83, TNF-alpha -0.41, CRP -0.67 (I2=80.8%); no pooled disease-activity or joint-count outcome reported
Disease activity SMD -0.88 (-1.38 to -0.38) across 9 studies, 388 pts, at low/very low GRADE certainty with selection bias and unstable RA medication as heterogeneity sources
10 RCTs: TJC SMD -0.39 (-0.74 to -0.05), 3 of 10 trials high quality
64 patients, uncontrolled, DAS28 and HAQ lower at 1 and 3 years vs pretreatment while remaining on DMARDs; pooled MSC safety across autoimmune indications gives AE RR 2.35 (0.58-9.58)
Clearest effect on depressed mood (MBCT depression SMD -0.72, -1.22 to -0.22) rather than pain or disease activity; unblindable with an active-control problem
One 58-patient 5-week RCT: significant improvement in pain on movement, pain at rest, sleep quality and DAS28; no effect on morning stiffness. Nothing since 2006
VAS pain MD -12.68 mm (-19.08 to -6.28) from 7 small studies; narrow therapeutic window

Cochrane 7 trials, 345 participants: pain MD -2.15 (-3.19 to -1.11), a 22% absolute improvement, but from 2 studies and 81 participants at very low quality; disease activity inconclusive; ~75% of trials did not report random sequence generation
8 RCTs, 1,209 pts: improved ACR20/50/70 as csDMARD add-on and reduced adverse effects, at limited methodological quality

10 trials, 1,185 pts vs NSAIDs: more improved patients and more RF disappearance (P<0.00001; P=0.008), better morning stiffness and ESR; no difference in swollen joints, grip strength or CRP. NSAID comparator cannot support a disease-modifying claim

Earlier treatment associates with better outcomes, but the strongest study is a 20-per-arm case-control, no RCT has randomised time-to-treatment, and the duration-response gradient is absent in smokers (BARFOT, n=1,587)

item: Whether ACPA-negative RA is one disease
statement: Different genetics and environmental associations; 10-year drug-free remission 26.6%, diagnosis change 12.8%; apparently preventable where ACPA-positive disease is not

No validated treatment-allocation tool exists. Synovial RNA-seq models reach AUC 0.75-0.87 for response and multidrug resistance but none has been prospectively tested as an allocation rule; drug selection remains sequential trial-and-error at 3-6 months per failed cycle
evidence_tier: Probable for prediction; no evidence for clinical utility

item: No intervention exists for response prediction
statement: Across 67 interventions in 12 traditions surveyed in Phase 2, zero address UN4. This is an empty intervention space, not a contested one

No patient who ever needed a bDMARD achieved sustained DMARD-free remission, versus 37% at 5 years of those who never did. Withdrawal trials are run in the population where DFR essentially never occurs

item: Why ACPA-negative at-risk disease appears preventable
statement: TREAT EARLIER 5-year: RA in 3/35 (9%) vs 10/31 (32%) in ACPA-negative at-risk participants, HR 0.24 (0.07-0.87), NNT 4; no effect in ACPA-positive. Single post-hoc subgroup, n=66

A stromal/fibroblast signature marks multidrug resistance; spatial data describe fibrogenic vascular niches with COMP-high fibroblasts and Notch-driven TGF-beta signalling expanding after immune depletion. Never tested interventionally

43% of difficult-to-treat patients have high disease activity scores without objective inflammation. They receive escalating immunosuppression with no mechanistic rationale and no established alternative
evidence_tier: Established as a phenomenon; no established treatment

item: True attributable fraction of modifiable exposure
statement: Population twin data: additive genetic variance 12% (0-76%), shared environment 50% (0-72%) — compatible with a far larger modifiable component than the commonly quoted ~60% heritability implies

item: Whether tolerance can be induced rather than immunity suppressed
statement: Peresolimab is the first clinical test of agonising an inhibitory checkpoint in RA; Treg and low-dose IL-2 approaches have reviews but no controlled RA efficacy trial; CAR-T experience in RA is minimal

item: Why the joint, and why symmetrically
statement: No current causal model explains the anatomical specificity or symmetry of RA

item: Causal direction of the gut-joint axis
statement: Dysbiosis reported in preclinical and established RA and partially normalised after treatment; causal direction unresolved. No RA efficacy trial of faecal microbiota transplantation or helminth therapy exists
Denosumab (erosion healing 20% vs 6%) is the only intervention in the entire survey addressing structural repair, and it does not affect inflammation
evidence_tier: Probable for one agent; unknown otherwise

statement: Only 2 of 67 interventions map to UN7, both incidentally. No intervention has been developed or tested for a defined RA subgroup

item: Whether sleep is a modifiable target
statement: 5 studies, 262 patients, no consistent or conclusive evidence, despite sleep disturbance being near-universal in RA
99 patients, mean 15.4 years' disease, >5 prior DMARDs: ACR response 28.9% vs 10.6% on sham (p=0.005; 41.7% vs 15.6% among completers). Withdrawn on cost and practicality as biologics arrived
evidence_tier: Probable (positive sham-controlled RCT, not replicated since)
reason: Abandoned despite positive controlled evidence

statement: 1980s-90s RCTs: improvement in 5 of 7 clinical measures and ESR. Never re-tested with modern methods or outcomes
reason: Abandoned despite positive controlled evidence

statement: >=ACR50 at some point in 49/76 (67%) with severe refractory disease; abandoned when biologics arrived, without a head-to-head comparison
reason: Abandoned without a comparison

item: Anakinra / IL-1 blockade in defined subgroups
statement: Cochrane-confirmed efficacy (ACR20 38% vs 23%) displaced by more effective agents on average. Whether an IL-1-driven subgroup exists has not been tested with modern stratification
evidence_tier: Established for average effect; hypothesis for subgroup
reason: Effective agent retired on average effect, subgroup never sought

statement: Pooled ACR20 RR 1.67 (1.40-2.00) in TNF-inadequate responders across 10 studies; class established in PsA and axSpA but not used in RA. No retrieved source documents why
reason: Anomaly: positive evidence, absent from practice

statement: Positive phase 3 ACR20 (40% vs 24%; 53.5%/54.8% vs placebo) without licensure; ocrelizumab DAS28 response RR 3.77 (2.47-5.74) with RA development stopped while the same molecule succeeded in MS
reason: Abandoned for non-efficacy reasons

statement: Open-label pilot, 16 patients, 4 days: DAS28-CRP 4.1->3.8 (p=0.02) in the high-activity cohort and no effect in the low-activity cohort. The implanted route now has a positive sham-controlled pivotal trial; the non-invasive route has never been sham-tested in RA
evidence_tier: Hypothesis (uncontrolled pilot) with a proven mechanism upstream
reason: Gap: proven mechanism, untested cheap route

statement: In a 94-patient double-blind elimination study negative on average, 9 patients improved and then flared markedly on rechallenge with changes in objective activity measures. Never retested in >30 years
evidence_tier: Hypothesis (rechallenge-defined subgroup within a negative trial)
reason: Subgroup signal inside a negative result

statement: 27 vs 26 patients: significant improvement in tender joints, Ritchie index, swollen joints, pain, morning stiffness, grip strength, ESR, CRP, white cell count and HAQ, sustained at one year, with only pain improving in controls. Single-blind, residential, unmatched control setting
evidence_tier: Uncertain (strongest historical dietary result, never adequately replicated)
reason: Abandoned line with an unusually broad positive result

statement: TREAT EARLIER 5-year post-hoc: HR 0.24 (0.07-0.87), NNT 4 in ACPA-negative at-risk participants where ACPA-positive showed nothing. n=66, post-hoc, never independently replicated
reason: Subgroup effect that inverts the main trial result

item: Never-bDMARD patients as the drug-free remission population
statement: 37% (5 y) vs 0% sustained DMARD-free remission depending only on whether a bDMARD was ever needed. Withdrawal trials have been run in the wrong population if this is a marker rather than a consequence
reason: Population-selection anomaly in the existing trial base

statement: Fibroblast COMP and endothelial Notch-driven TGF-beta signalling expand after immune depletion in non-remitting patients. If disease becomes stromally autonomous, no immune-targeted drug can resolve it
reason: Untested gap with a specific mechanistic prediction

statement: 43% of difficult-to-treat patients have no objective inflammation, higher BMI and 15-38% fibromyalgia prevalence, and currently receive escalating immunosuppression. No trial has randomised a non-immunosuppressive strategy in an imaging-defined NIRRA population
evidence_tier: Established as a phenomenon; no intervention tested
reason: Untested gap affecting a defined and identifiable group

item: Total glucosides of paeony as a tolerability agent
statement: Reported to improve ACR responses and reduce adverse effects when added to csDMARDs. The adverse-effect reduction is the less studied of the two claims and maps to a top patient priority
reason: Outcome that matters to patients, reported incidentally

statement: Largest non-Western RCT base in the survey (31 RCTs, 2,776 pts; ACR70 RR 2.19 at GRADE high certainty as MTX add-on) and essentially unknown in Western practice; no independent non-Chinese/Japanese trial retrieved
reason: Effective agent absent from one hemisphere's practice

item: Whether TwHF's active constituents can be separated from gonadal toxicity
statement: Efficacy comparable to methotrexate with a 40-year reproductive toxicology record. The efficacy and the toxicity have not been attributed to the same or different constituents in the retrieved evidence
evidence_tier: Probable for efficacy; established concern for toxicity
reason: Effective agent limited by a possibly separable harm

statement: Whether same-acupoint sham is an inert control is an empirical question that determines whether a large body of positive evidence is real or artefactual, and it has not been settled by any retrieved study
reason: Conflict whose resolution is a study design, not a treatment

item: Helminth therapy and faecal microbiota transplantation
statement: Both follow directly from the mucosal-origins hypothesis; neither has any RA efficacy trial
reason: Untested gap downstream of an established observation

statement: The approaches most directly aimed at drug-free remission have the thinnest RA clinical evidence base of any modern strategy — reviews only, no controlled RA trial
reason: Highest-priority need, lowest evidence density

statement: CD19xCD3 bispecific engager on compassionate use in 6 multidrug-resistant patients: rapid decline in disease activity in all six, activated memory B cells replaced by IgD+ naive B cells, no clinically relevant CRS
reason: Early uncontrolled signal in the population with fewest options

statement: Near-universal symptom, 5 studies and 262 patients in total, no conclusion possible
reason: Untested gap in a top patient-priority domain

item: RA-specific cannabinoid and low-dose naltrexone data
statement: LDN is negative for pain overall (d=-0.11) with a positive fibromyalgia subgroup (d=-0.34), and ~34% of RA patients meet fibromyalgia criteria. Cannabis has one 58-patient RA trial from 2006. Both are used off-label without RA-specific evidence
reason: Widespread off-label use with no RA evidence base
source: LDN meta-analysis; Sativex RCT; FM prevalence cohort
